question.text: A fighter jet is flying horizontally at a certain altitude with a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. When it passes directly overhead an anti-aircraft gun, a bullet is fired from the gun, at an angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>θ</mi></math> with the horizontal, to hit the jet. If the bullet speed is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>400</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>θ</mi></math> will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>°</mo></math>.

solution.text:
In order to hit, horizontal velocity of both moving object should be same,

V1=V2cosθ ⇒200=400cosθ

⇒cosθ=12 ⇒θ=60°
